name: old asphalt road: mostly one dark warm charcoal tone with an even fine grain of mid-grey aggregate, soft low-frequency paler wheel-worn zones that flow across tiles, rare dark and rare light aggregate pixels; its unconnected edges are a chipped broken rim 1 to 3 pixels deep that varies continuously along the road, lighter broken faces on the far (north) rim, irregular rounded-off ends at dead ends and outer corners, and a dry dark-brown ledge 1 to 2 pixels thick with a broken soil shadow on the south side; laid as a road network with crossroads, dead ends and long straight 1-wide and 3-wide runs (cracks and potholes are separate decals)

surfaces.part: asphalt road patches on dirt ground (flat terrain tiles)

answer.evidence: The image is a flat top-down terrain sheet: dark asphalt road shapes on a brown dirt ground. The roads have chipped rims, a lighter north rim and a thin 1-2 px dark-brown ledge on the south edge. This is a ground ledge, not a vertical front face of 3+ rows. No standing volume, front face or elevated horizontal surface is drawn, which is expected for terrain tiles. The width profile is a constant 368 across all rows because the dirt background fills the full sheet.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 3 visible tones per 16x16 tile, with 9 distinct colours in total. The paving reference shows 7 tones and the grass reference shows 3 tones but with varied clumps. Near-flat coverage is 55%, against 0% for both references, so over half the image is flat fill. The road bodies are large areas of one charcoal tone with sparse light aggregate dots. The aggregate is not an even fine grain, and I see no soft paler wheel-worn zones flowing across tiles. The soil surround is also mostly flat brown with sparse speckle. The edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the rim is tinted rather than a black sticker outline, which is a plus. The rim reads as a thin lighter lip with a darker ledge, but it is mostly uniform, with little chipped variation, and the ledge and soil shadow are barely visible. Overall, material depth is shallow: about 3 steps against roughly 5-6 for Beodeul.
